reason: Pharaoh, the Egyptian leader in this passage, demonstrates no moral accountability for the Hebrew people's welfare. Rather than taking responsibility for their wellbeing, he actively oppresses them by commanding their midwives to commit infanticide (killing male babies at birth). When this method fails—because the midwives fear God and allow the boys to live—Pharaoh escalates rather than reconsiders his approach. He then orders all his people to drown Hebrew male infants in the Nile. Throughout, Pharaoh views the Hebrew population growth as a threat to be controlled through violent suppression, not as people for whose condition he bears any moral responsibility. His actions reveal a complete absence of accountability toward the Hebrew people; he seeks only to manage and diminish them.
